notes: SHIP v1.14.431 - SITE SETUP, THE GUIDED FIRST-RUN FLOW (spec section 4.1). WHY THIS SHIPPED BEFORE THE BOOT GATE, WHICH IS WHAT WAS ASKED FOR. Spec section 3 routes a first run to Site Setup, and that destination did not exist. rd_openProfile is a profile EDITOR - text inputs and textareas, no Master step anywhere in it - so gating against it would have sent a fresh device to a form that never mentions a Master, leaving the operator to go find the importer themselves. That is worse than the current behaviour of landing on Home with everything reachable. The gate is the last ten percent of a feature whose first ninety percent was missing; this is that ninety percent. WHAT IT IS. Welcome, Site, Site Lead, Operator defaulting to the Site Lead and editable, then Master. Five steps, Back and Next, a step dot row, and both controls consuming the 44px floor as their OWN height rather than being sized by a sibling. It reuses the existing sheet primitive so it is one more sheet in a family rather than a new visual language - polish is step 7 of the programme and no visual redesign lands before step 4 completes. THE MASTER STEP IMPORTS NOTHING ITSELF. It calls master_loadFromPicker, the one door, which already parses, stages, validates, shows the counts summary and activates on a tap. Section 4.2 is explicit that there is no second write path to Master state anywhere in the file, and the entire SINGLE-MASTER arc exists because of what a second writer costs. The flow detects ACTIVATION rather than assuming it: the picker resolves with the parse result whether or not the operator activated, so setup compares PHANTOM_MASTER.id() across the call. Cancelled or refused leaves setup open on the Master step to try another file. ORDER IS DELIBERATE. Identity is saved BEFORE the picker so a mid-import abort still leaves the operator their typing - the same persist-first discipline the SINGLE-MASTER LAW applies to the Master, applied to the cheaper half. confirmedAt is NOT written there: the profile counts as confirmed only once a Master is genuinely active, so an abandoned setup can never present itself as a finished one. A REAL DEFECT FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, AND IT WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE GATE. siteProfile_save stamps lastUpdated on EVERY save, and siteProfile_load backfills confirmedAt from lastUpdated whenever confirmedAt is absent. That v1.6.70 rule reads saved via the editor means a human confirmed it, which was true while the editor was the only caller. Site Setup is a second caller whose mid-flow save is explicitly NOT a confirmation - so without a change, a device that opened setup, typed a site and quit would read back CONFIRMED and satisfy a confirmedAt-based boot gate with NO MASTER behind it. Precisely the state the gate exists to catch. The backfill now skips a profile carrying setupInProgress, which setup sets on its in-flight save and deletes when a Master goes live. Existing devices carry no marker and are completely unaffected - pinned by test in BOTH directions, because breaking the other half would re-prompt every device in the field. TESTS: new spec 21-site-setup, eleven tests - the five steps in spec order, the operator defaulting to the lead and remaining editable, typing surviving a Back tap, the Master step blocked until identity is set, confirmedAt withheld until a Master is active, both halves of the backfill exception, merge-never-overwrite on empty fields, pre-fill making the flow re-runnable from SYSTEM, the one-door assertion that setup never parses or stages or activates by itself, and a real entry point that cannot compose in the legacy house. 21 plus 10-site-profile-root: 27 passed. TWO OF THE FIRST THREE FAILURES WERE THE TEST, NOT THE CODE - the fixture boots a CONFIGURED device, so first-run assertions were being made against a device that already had an operator and a confirmation, and the code was right to decline to overwrite either. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep. ?legacy=1 unaffected - the sheet is body.rd plus .open gated and its door is redesign-only. DEVICE-VERIFY: none required for the flow itself, which is fully harness-covered. The boot gate that routes a first run here is the NEXT ship and that one will want a device pass.
